prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original material illustration atlas for a Chinese talking-head explainer, never applied to the person. Create a square 2 by 2 atlas of FOUR SEPARATE hand-painted thick oil impasto miniatures on separate small ivory canvas fragments. Order: top-left a simple shopping tote bag, top-right two overlapping generic blank coins, bottom-left a shield with one simple checkmark, bottom-right a heavy compact iron weight with one round lifting hole. All four subjects are original conceptual symbols, no brands, no currency denominations, no numbers, no writing. Strong physical paint material: thick opaque pigment deposited by a palette knife, distinctly raised ridges and broken bristle furrows, visible overlapping masses, consistently raking light from upper left giving tiny ridge shadows. Bag russet and cream, coins ochre, shield muted forest green, weight deep blue-gray. Flat-on camera, no perspective warping of entire paintings. Paint ridges must visibly build the actual object forms, NOT a texture overlay on smooth vector icons, NOT plastic clay sculptures. Four complete miniatures entirely separated with at least 12 percent empty transparent gap both vertically and horizontally and wide transparent exterior margin. Transparent background outside each canvas fragment, preserve real pigment edge irregularity within each fragment. No titles, panels, framing graphics, watermarks, hands, people or tools. This is a carefully lit photograph-like rendering of original imaginary painted surfaces, not a claim of a real artwork or named artist. Each complete fragment fits within its quadrant with generous safe margin, never touches or crosses the central gap.

Use case: stylized-concept. Make an original square 2 by 2 material atlas, FOUR separate modern lacquer plaques isolated on transparent background, each complete plaque with wide transparent margin and a wide empty central cross so quadrants can be separated. Each plaque is a thin deep black-red polished lacquer square with gently rounded corners, seen nearly straight-on; subtle edge thickness and a small controlled reflection at upper left prove the rich glossy surface. On these four lacquer surfaces depict ORIGINAL fine gold line and irregular gold-powder illustrations, thin restrained gold with varying particle density, NEVER chunky solid gold objects: top-left a shopping tote bag, top-right two generic overlapping blank coins, bottom-left a shield with a plain checkmark, bottom-right a compact lifting weight with circular hole. All motifs fully inside their own plaque and legible. Curves and negative space are elegant and sparse, no ornament unrelated to these four objects. Vary the gold powder density within the motif areas; the lacquer plane stays dark and smooth. Warm edge reflections confined to lacquer, no overall haze. This is a modern original conceptual lacquer illustration, not an actual antique, not an artisan's authentic work, not a procedural demonstration. No signature, seals, Chinese characters, text, numerals, logos, hands, people, gradient background or watermark. Make real material distinctions between thin gold marks resting on lacquer and the deep polished ground. At least 12 percent transparent gaps between plaques and generous transparent outer margin; absolutely no plate edge cropped.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: original square 2 by 2 atlas of four separate modern vitreous enamel pin-like badges on a true transparent background. Top-left badge silhouette is a simple shopping tote bag, top-right two overlapping generic blank coin circles, bottom-left a shield with one clear checkmark, bottom-right a compact heavy weight with circular hole. Each item is a small physical metal-backed object with a narrow raised warm brass outer rim, a few precisely fitted internal metal divisions, visibly glossy colored enamel pools with subtle meniscus inside the cells. Palette muted coral, deep teal, ivory, warm ochre; restrained sidewall thickness and small clean reflections from an upper-left softbox. Nearly front-facing slight three-quarter view enough to see metal thickness without distorting symbols. Every cell is contained by metal, no floating paint or broken ribs. These are SOLID opaque colored enamel objects, not transparent stained glass windows, not white porcelain plates, not flat vector icons or 3D plastic toys. Four objects are completely independent, no contact with one another, each fits comfortably inside its own quadrant. A wide empty transparent center cross of at least 12 percent canvas width and wide outer transparent margin prevent any clipping. No lettering, numbers, currency marks, logos, signatures, paper cards, hands, people, watermarks, backdrop or extra objects. Original modern concept objects, no reference to actual medals, institutions or historic artifacts.

Each panel is a genuinely assembled backlit colored-glass artwork: thick dark lead cames form connected closed boundaries, pieces of softly textured colored translucent glass held within them, subtle ripples/bubbles and bright transmitted daylight show glass material. Panel subjects in fixed order: top-left shopping tote bag, top-right two overlapping generic blank coin discs, bottom-left shield with simple checkmark, bottom-right compact heavy lifting weight with a circular hole.
